args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failing health checks, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks, with error rate at 18% and service healthy=false. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production status (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was not a candidate). The initial rollback halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed-version state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). The rollback was retried and completed successfully across all three regions. Verified post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up: investigate root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures and the transient orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout.

trace.final:
The incident did land (INC-0001) — the timeout was on the response, not the write, so I did not retry.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on **v2.3.1** in all three production regions with `healthy: false` and an 18% error rate. Release history showed the most recent production-healthy version was **v2.3.0**; `v2.3.1-rc` was staging-only *and* unhealthy, so it was not a valid rollback target.

**Rollback:** The first rollback attempt failed partway with `partial_failure: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1). I retried the rollback and it completed with `rolled_out` across all three regions. Verified afterward: us-east, us-west, and eu-west all on **v2.3.0**, `healthy: true`, error rate down to **0.2%**.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on checkout-api — open, with a summary covering the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback to v2.3.0, the transient partial-rollout error and retry, and the verified recovery.

Two things worth flagging for follow-up (noted in the incident): the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is still unknown, and the orchestrator error that halted the first rollout may warrant investigation since it left production split across two versions for a period.
